meta.audience: Nephi and Lehi, and then the Lamanites
meta.location: Zarahemla, the land southward, and the prison in the land of Nephi
meta.unit: The rise of the Gadianton band (Helaman 1–6)
principles: A name given as a reminder

world_behind.title: Nephi resigns the judgment-seat
world_behind.text: Verses 1 and 4 have him handing it to Cezoram and taking up preaching for the rest of his life, along with his brother Lehi.

world_behind.title: The reason is the electorate
world_behind.text: Verse 2 says the laws and government rested on the voice of the people, and that those who chose evil had become the majority.

world_behind.title: Helaman's charge is quoted whole
world_behind.text: Verses 6 through 12 are his words to his sons, remembered years afterward and reproduced by Mormon.

world_behind.title: The charge cites two earlier sermons
world_behind.text: Verse 9 sends them to Benjamin's words in Mosiah 3, and verse 10 to Amulek's answer to Zeezrom in Alma 11.

world_behind.title: The mission runs city by city
world_behind.text: Verses 14 through 16 trace it from Bountiful to Gid to Mulek, through the land southward, and then into Zarahemla among the Lamanites.

world_behind.title: The prison is a named place
world_behind.text: Verse 21 identifies it as the same prison where Ammon and his brethren were held by the servants of Limhi, in Mosiah 7.

world_behind.title: Aminadab is a Nephite dissenter
world_behind.text: Verse 35 says he had once belonged to the church, and verse 41 has him naming Alma, Amulek, and Zeezrom as the teachers the Lamanites had heard.

words.text: Coming to the point of harvest. The record uses the word four times, all of them in Helaman, at 5:2, 6:40, 8:26, and 11:37. The King James Bible has it once, at Isaiah 18:5.
Arrows. The word occurs once in scripture, here, in the phrase "his shafts in the whirlwind." It sits between the devil's mighty winds and his hail and storm.
Treated at Alma 7:10, of the Spirit and Mary. The record uses the word nine times, and six of them are in this chapter, all of the cloud of darkness in the prison.
Gentleness, absence of force. Both of the record's uses are in this chapter, at verses 30 and 31, and the King James Bible has neither. Verse 30 attaches it to a voice that pierced to the soul.
Unable to be moved. The record uses the word five times, at 1 Nephi 2:10 of a valley, at Mosiah 5:15 and Alma 1:25 of people who hold firm, and here of men held still by fear.
Beyond words. The record uses it three times and the King James Bible three, including Peter's "joy unspeakable and full of glory," which verse 44 repeats almost exactly.

phrases.term: They who chose evil were more numerous than they who chose good
phrases.text: The diagnosis behind Nephi's resignation. Mosiah 29 had warned that a government by the voice of the people depends on what that voice chooses.

phrases.term: Nephi had become weary because of their iniquity
phrases.text: The record gives the reason a chief judge quit. He leaves the seat and spends the rest of his days preaching.

phrases.term: When you remember your names ye may remember them
phrases.text: Helaman's stated purpose in naming his sons Nephi and Lehi. The chain runs from name to person to works to the written record that they were good.

phrases.term: That ye may do these things to lay up for yourselves a treasure in heaven
phrases.text: The motive he asks for, set against doing good in order to boast. He adds that the treasure is eternal and does not fade.

phrases.term: To redeem them from their sins
phrases.text: Helaman quoting Amulek at Zeezrom. The distinction between rescue in sin and rescue out of it is the point of the citation.

phrases.term: It is upon the rock of our Redeemer, who is Christ, the Son of God, that ye must build your foundation
phrases.text: The center of the charge. Everything before it is memory and everything after it is weather.

phrases.term: A foundation whereon if men build they cannot fall
phrases.text: The promise stated at its plainest. The winds, shafts, hail, and storm are all granted, and the outcome is fixed anyway.

phrases.term: Even in that same prison in which Ammon and his brethren were cast by the servants of Limhi
phrases.text: Mormon locating the cell. The record has used this building before, and naming it links two generations of missionaries in one room.

phrases.term: It was a still voice of perfect mildness, as if it had been a whisper, and it did pierce even to the very soul
phrases.text: The verse the chapter is remembered for. The earth shakes and the walls tremble around a voice too quiet to shout over.

phrases.term: They do converse with the angels of God
phrases.text: Aminadab's answer to the question of the multitude. A dissenter names what is happening because he recognizes it.

phrases.term: As many as were convinced did lay down their weapons of war, and also their hatred and the tradition of their fathers
phrases.text: Three things surrendered together. Alma 24 had the weapons buried, and this verse adds the hatred and the tradition.

verses.label: v. 1–4
verses.title: The seat given up
verses.text: Nephi delivers the judgment-seat to Cezoram. The laws rest on the voice of the people, those who chose evil outnumber those who chose good, the laws are corrupt, and the people are stiffnecked past governing. Weary of their iniquity, Nephi resigns and takes up preaching with Lehi for the rest of their lives.

verses.label: v. 5–8
verses.title: The charge remembered
verses.text: They act because they remember their father's words. Helaman had asked them to keep the commandments and to declare his words, and had explained their names: remember the names, and you remember the men, and their works, and that the record calls them good. He asks that their own good be done for a treasure in heaven.

verses.label: v. 9–12
verses.title: Remember
verses.text: He points them to Benjamin's teaching that salvation comes only through the atoning blood of Christ, and to Amulek's answer that Christ redeems people from their sins rather than in them, on condition of repentance. Then he gives the rock: build on the Redeemer, and the devil's winds, shafts, hail, and storm cannot drag you down.

verses.label: v. 13–20
verses.title: The mission
verses.text: They remember and go, beginning at Bountiful, then Gid, then Mulek, through every city of the land southward, and into Zarahemla among the Lamanites. They confound many Nephite dissenters, who confess, are baptized, and return to repair the wrongs they had done. Preaching with power and authority, and given what to say, they baptize eight thousand Lamanites.

verses.label: v. 21–27
verses.title: The prison and the fire
verses.text: Going on to the land of Nephi, they are taken and imprisoned in the cell where Ammon had been held. After many days without food their captors come to kill them and find them encircled as if by fire, unburned. The Lamanites stand struck dumb. Nephi and Lehi tell them not to fear, and the earth shakes and the prison walls shake without falling.

verses.label: v. 28–41
verses.title: The cloud and the voice
verses.text: A cloud of darkness overshadows them with an awful solemn fear. A voice calls twice for repentance and once speaks words that cannot be uttered, and each time the earth shakes. They cannot flee or move. Aminadab, a Nephite dissenter, turns and sees the faces of Nephi and Lehi shining like angels' and lifted toward heaven. He calls the multitude to look, and tells them the two are conversing with angels and that they must repent and cry to the voice until they have faith in Christ.

verses.label: v. 42–52
verses.title: The answer
verses.text: They cry until the cloud disperses, and find every soul encircled by a pillar of fire that does no harm. The Holy Spirit enters their hearts, and a pleasant voice like a whisper speaks peace because of their faith in the Well Beloved. The heavens open and angels minister to about three hundred souls, who go out and declare what they saw. Most of the Lamanites are convinced, lay down their weapons, their hatred, and their traditions, and give the Nephites back their lands.

chapter.title: A chief judge resigns over the electorate
chapter.text: Verse 2 gives the reason as a majority that chooses evil. Nephi concludes that the office can no longer do what preaching might.

chapter.title: The charge is built on memory
chapter.text: Helaman uses "remember" eight times in seven verses, and his instrument is the boys' own names.

chapter.title: Two sermons are handed forward by citation
chapter.text: Benjamin in Mosiah 3 and Amulek in Alma 11 are named and quoted. The record shows its own teaching passing down as quoted text.

chapter.title: The rock is given with the storm attached
chapter.text: Verse 12 grants the winds, the shafts, the hail, and the mighty storm, and places the promise past them rather than instead of them.

chapter.title: The prison is the same building as Mosiah 7
chapter.text: Mormon connects two sets of missionaries across roughly a century by naming the cell.

chapter.title: Nephites and Lamanites are in the darkness together
chapter.text: Verse 27 says those in the prison were Lamanites and Nephite dissenters. The cloud does not sort them.

chapter.title: The turning point comes from a dissenter
chapter.text: Aminadab knows what he is looking at because he once belonged to the church, and he names the teachers the Lamanites had already heard.

chapter.title: Land is returned as a consequence of conversion
chapter.text: Verse 52 has the Lamanites yielding up the lands they had taken in Helaman 4. The military loss is reversed by preaching.

applications.title: Leave the seat you cannot use
applications.text: Nephi judged that preaching would do what the office no longer could. Changing what you are doing is sometimes the honest response to a job that has stopped working.

applications.title: Attach a reminder to something you carry
applications.text: Helaman used his sons' names. Tie the thing you want remembered to something already in daily use.

applications.title: Grant the storm and keep the foundation
applications.text: The promise does not include better weather. Assume the winds and ask what you are standing on.

applications.title: Say what you already know when someone asks
applications.text: Aminadab was a lapsed member in a dark room, and his answer turned three hundred people. What you know is useful even when you feel disqualified.

questions.text: Where am I in the majority, and what is it choosing?
What am I weary of, and what would I do instead?
What was I named after, and does it work on me?
Am I doing this good thing so that it can be said of me?
What am I built on, and have I checked it in a storm?
When did a quiet correction reach me that a loud one could not?
What hatred or inherited habit would I have to lay down along with the weapon?

entries.head: Hel. 3:21

anchor.quote: I have given unto you the names of our first parents who came out of the land of Jerusalem

entries.reason: the naming itself, reported when the sons were born

targets.quote: He gave unto the eldest the name of Nephi, and unto the youngest, the name of Lehi.
targets.verse_text: And it came to pass that he had two sons. He gave unto the eldest the name of Nephi, and unto the youngest, the name of Lehi. And they began to grow up unto the Lord.
targets.markdown: And it came to pass that he had two sons. **He gave unto the eldest the name of Nephi, and unto the youngest, the name of Lehi**. And they began to grow up unto the Lord.

targets.quote: they had altered and trampled under their feet the laws of Mosiah,
targets.verse_text: And that they had altered and trampled under their feet the laws of Mosiah, or that which the Lord commanded him to give unto the people; and they saw that their laws had become corrupted, and that they had become a wicked people, insomuch that they were wicked even like unto the Lamanites.
